---
title: "RTM behaviour (interactive)"
---

```{python}
from _lib import *
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from leafrtm.rtm import get_model
import yaml

pri = yaml.safe_load(open(ROOT / "config" / "priors.yaml"))["rtm"]


def prior_quantiles(p, qs=(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95)):
    from scipy import stats
    s = pri[p]
    if s["dist"] == "lognormal":
        return [float(np.exp(s["meanlog"] + s["sdlog"] * stats.norm.ppf(q))) for q in qs]
    if s["dist"] == "truncnormal":
        lo = (s.get("lower", -np.inf) - s["mu"]) / s["sigma"]
        hi = (s.get("upper", np.inf) - s["mu"]) / s["sigma"]
        return [float(stats.truncnorm(lo, hi, s["mu"], s["sigma"]).ppf(q)) for q in qs]
    return [s["lower"] + q * (s["upper"] - s["lower"]) for q in qs]


def sensitivity(model_name, base, height=480):
    """One dropdown entry per parameter; slider steps over its prior 5-95 % quantiles."""
    m = get_model(model_name)
    qs = (0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95)
    blues = ["#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#2a78d6", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b"]
    fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, horizontal_spacing=0.08)
    vis_by_param = []
    for pi, p in enumerate(m.params):
        vals = prior_quantiles(p, qs)
        start = len(fig.data)
        for k, v in enumerate(vals):
            R, T = m.simulate({**base, p: v})
            for col, y in ((1, R), (2, T)):
                fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=m.wavelength, y=y, mode="lines", line=dict(color=blues[k], width=2),
                                         name=f"{p} = {v:.3g} (prior q{int(qs[k]*100):02d})",
                                         legendgroup=f"{p}{k}", showlegend=(col == 1), visible=(pi == 0),
                                         hovertemplate=f"{p} = {v:.3g}<br>" + "%{x} nm: %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>"),
                              1, col)
        vis_by_param.append(range(start, len(fig.data)))
    n = len(fig.data)
    buttons = []
    for pi, p in enumerate(m.params):
        vis = [False] * n
        for i in vis_by_param[pi]:
            vis[i] = True
        buttons.append(dict(label=p, method="update", args=[{"visible": vis}]))
    fig.update_layout(updatemenus=[dict(buttons=buttons, x=0, y=1.02, xanchor="left", yanchor="bottom", direction="right",
                                        type="buttons", showactive=True)],
                      height=height, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.2))
    fig.update_xaxes(title_text="wavelength (nm)")
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="reflectance", col=1)
    fig.update_yaxes(title_text="transmittance", col=2)
    return fig
```

These figures show how each RTM responds to its parameters. Pick a parameter with the
buttons. Each line is the spectrum at one quantile of that parameter's prior (5, 25, 50, 75
and 95 %), with all other parameters at their prior medians. Parameters that move the
spectrum strongly, and in a distinctive place, are the ones the data can inform; compare the
[identifiability diagnostics](a-diagnostics.qmd).

## PROSPECT-D

```{python}
base = dict(N=1.5, Cab=40, Car=10, Canth=2, Cbrown=0.1, Cw=0.01, Cm=0.009)
show(sensitivity("prospectd", base))
```

## PROSPECT-PRO

PRO splits dry matter into protein and carbon-based constituents, which absorb in different
SWIR bands.

```{python}
base = dict(N=1.5, Cab=40, Car=10, Canth=2, Cbrown=0.1, Cw=0.01, Cprot=0.0012, Ccbc=0.007)
show(sensitivity("prospectpro", base))
```

## LIBERTY

LIBERTY's structure parameters work differently from PROSPECT's single $\mathcal{N}$. The
intercellular air space $x_u$ controls internal scattering, "thickness" stacks layers, and
the baseline absorption raises absorption at every wavelength. Strong scattering combined
with weak absorption leaves LIBERTY undefined: its $R_\infty$ equation has no real root. Bright
leaves push fits against that edge; see [LIBERTY's valid region](a-liberty.qmd).

```{python}
base = dict(xu=0.03, thick=1.6, baseline=0.0005, element=2, c_factor=200, w_factor=100, l_factor=40, p_factor=1)
show(sensitivity("liberty", base))
```

## LeafSIP

LeafSIP has no $\mathcal{N}$. Dry matter $C_m$ sets both the absorption normalization and the
structural parameters $p$ (recollision probability) and $q$ (asymmetry). LMA therefore
controls both chemistry and structure.

```{python}
base = dict(Cab=40, Car=10, Canth=2, Cbrown=0.1, Cw=0.01, Cm=0.009)
show(sensitivity("leafsip", base))
```

## Absorption coefficients

The versions differ mainly in their specific absorption coefficients. Use the legend to
toggle traces.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Specific absorption coefficients by constituent and model (log scale; zero values not shown). PROSPECT units: cm² µg⁻¹ for pigments, cm⁻¹ for water, cm² g⁻¹ for dry matter; LIBERTY units follow Dawson et al. (1998)."
CONST_COLOR = {"Cab": "#2a78d6", "Car": "#eb6834", "Canth": "#1baf7a", "Cbrown": "#eda100",
               "Cw": "#e87ba4", "Cm": "#008300", "Cprot": "#6250d6", "Ccbc": "#52514e"}
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=["PROSPECT versions", "LIBERTY"], horizontal_spacing=0.08)
for mname, dash in (("prospect4", "dot"), ("prospect5", "dash"), ("prospectd", "solid"), ("prospectpro", "dashdot")):
    m = get_model(mname)
    for j, c in enumerate(m.constituents):
        k = m.K[:, j]
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=m.wavelength, y=np.where(k > 0, k, np.nan), mode="lines",
                                 name=f"{MODEL_LABEL[mname]} {c}", line=dict(width=1.5, dash=dash,
                                 color=CONST_COLOR[c]),
                                 visible=True if mname == "prospectd" else "legendonly"), 1, 1)
lib = get_model("liberty")
for j, c in enumerate(["chlorophyll", "water", "albino", "lignin+cellulose", "protein"]):
    k = lib.K[:, j]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=lib.wavelength, y=np.where(k > 0, k, np.nan), mode="lines", name=f"LIBERTY {c}",
                             line=dict(width=1.5, color=list(MODEL_COLOR.values())[j % 7])), 1, 2)
fig.update_yaxes(type="log")
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="wavelength (nm)")
fig.update_layout(height=480, legend=dict(font=dict(size=10)))
show(fig)
```
